question: Does the evidence report distinguish unreviewed results and preserve the exact small artifacts and source versions needed to audit the experiments?
hypothesis: Separate result/review statuses and an archive built and verified from the same captured bytes prevent false review labels and digest/archive races. Explicit historical Git blobs preserve the actual trainer and diagnostic code alongside current code.

sources.sections: Claims, limitations, experimental reproducibility, code/data instructions and compute resources (items1,2,4,5,8)
sources.consequence: Separate measured outcomes, reviewed interpretation and unachieved targets. Retain exact code/environment/commands and failed or preliminary evidence; disclose large local dependencies rather than claiming a standalone dataset release.

sources.sections: TarFile.addfile, extractfile and regular-file member types
sources.consequence: Hash the same captured bytes supplied to addfile. Verify all archive members and manifest digests by reading file objects, without filesystem extraction or following links.

sources.sections: Batch input/output, object type/size and raw blob contents
sources.consequence: Read pinned regular-file blobs by object ID, preserving exact contents independently of current worktree changes and archive export attributes.

sources.sections: Named tree/commit archives and export attributes
sources.consequence: A source revision must be explicit; use raw blobs for byte identity rather than assuming the current worktree or export-filtered archive is the executed source.

differences: Local audit bundle only, not a paper submission, independent reproduction or public release. Large datasets/checkpoints remain local with existing lineage hashes. The current report has already been inspected: it can label an unreviewed result passed, omits raw diagnostic text/scripts, and hashes files before reading them again into the archive.
contrary_evidence: Checksums establish artifact consistency, not scientific validity or complete provenance. A finite bundle cannot include every system dependency; archived historical source may still require the recorded external data and environment. Fixing the report cannot supply missing experiments or reviews.

protocol.scope: Evidence reporter and reproducibility archive only. No training/evaluation protocol, source used by running jobs, or existing result/review is changed.
protocol.status: Keep measured result status separate from verified review status. Missing review is explicitly awaiting_literature_review, never passed. Reject stale/incomplete reviews using the existing gate against captured result bytes.
protocol.capture: Capture selected small regular files once; derive displayed evidence, hashes and tar members from those bytes. Include raw diagnostic .txt/.log and .py/.sh scripts as well as JSON/JSONL/NPZ evidence. Exclude large checkpoints/corpora, installed tools, previous report directories and the current output directory; preserve existing bundles by requiring a new output directory.
protocol.source: Include current source/config/docs/tests/environment files and optional explicitly named historical commits under pinned_sources/full_commit. Read regular-file blobs through Git, not worktree state or export filters. Include original trainer7dfc837, original diagnostic161fe8b and frozen camera-slot98e6fcf in the actual audit bundle.
protocol.integrity: Manifest hashes every included payload. Read the complete produced archive to reject duplicate/nonregular/unsafe members, missing/extra payloads or digest mismatches before publishing the final archive filename. No extraction to the filesystem. Record archive digest and file count separately.
protocol.verification: Targeted tests for unreviewed versus reviewed status, stale review rejection, raw text/script inclusion and large-artifact exclusion, source changes during archive writing, historical source identity, and corrupt/duplicate member rejection. Build one interim bundle from actual evidence and independently verify its members and known source/diagnostic contents. Revisit sources and review this software/artifact result before final use.
protocol.limits: At most64MiB per selected small file and256MiB total captured payload; fail visibly rather than silently omitting a selected file. Original checkpoint/corpus exclusion remains explicit. An interim evidence snapshot is not the final P25/P26 report.

success: Targeted fault-injection tests and actual archive verification pass, known raw diagnostics and three historical source versions are present, and unreviewed outcomes cannot appear as reviewed passes.
stop: Stop on an invalid/stale review, oversized selected payload, missing Git revision or archive mismatch; retain failure evidence. Never generate a scientific review or mark pending experiments complete to make the archive pass.
